q.t: Independence Day marks…
q.e: Independence Day (15 August) celebrates freedom from foreign rule.

q.t: Republic Day marks…
q.e: Republic Day (26 January) marks the rules by which India governs itself.

q.t: The saffron band on the flag stands for…
q.e: Saffron (top) = strength and courage.

q.t: The white band stands for…
q.e: White (middle) = peace and truth.

q.t: The green band stands for…
q.e: Green (bottom) = growth and prosperity.

q.t: The Ashoka Chakra stands for…
q.e: The blue wheel stands for dharma — duty.

q.t: The National Emblem shows…
q.e: Three lions on a circular platform, with the Ashoka Chakra below.

q.t: Wild Asiatic lions live only in…
q.e: Careful protection brought their numbers back to several hundred.

q.t: About how many languages are spoken in India?
q.e: More than a thousand languages, each with its own stories and songs.

q.t: UPI is…
q.e: UPI is the world's largest digital payment system.

q.t: Why does a note have a hidden watermark of Gandhiji?
o: It's built into the paper and hard to copy
q.e: A watermark can't be printed later, so it proves the note is genuine.

q.t: Why do notes have raised marks?
o: So people who can't see can tell them apart by touch
q.e: Good design works for everyone who must use it.

q.t: Which app reads out the value of a note?
q.e: The MANI app identifies currency notes aloud.

q.t: A symbol works only if…
q.e: A symbol nobody recognises is just a picture.

q.t: India's Constitution is…
o: The longest written constitution in the world
q.e: It is the longest written constitution of any country.

q.t: Why are there two national days, not one?
o: Freedom and the rules that make freedom work are different
q.e: Independence answered 'who decides'; the Constitution answered 'how we decide'.

q.t: Why does a forest survive without help, but a garden of one plant can fail?
o: In a forest different living things do each other's work
q.e: Variety is the working system — one disease can end a one-plant garden.

q.t: Why are drums so different across India?
o: Each region used its own local materials and music
They were designed by one person
q.e: Different wood, clay, hides and music shaped each region's drum.

q.t: Cloth wrapped round the head in a desert mainly…
q.e: Much headgear is practical — protecting from heat or cold.

q.t: The mridangam belongs to…
q.e: Mridangam is Carnatic; sitar and shehnai are Hindustani.

q.t: Freedom does not mean everyone can do whatever they like, because…
o: A country with no rules is unsafe for the weakest
q.e: Rules protect people so freedom can work.

q.t: Why did Republic Day come about two and a half years after Independence?
o: Writing the Constitution took that long
q.e: The rulebook took that long to write and agree.

q.t: When a language is lost, what is lost?
o: Songs, stories and ideas only ever said in it
q.e: A language carries a whole culture, not just labels.

q.t: Translation apps can't fully replace learning a language because…
o: They can't tell you how a word feels to a speaker
q.e: The best reason to learn another language is to understand, not just be understood.

q.t: Lion numbers rose from a few dozen to several hundred because of…
q.e: Protection of the Gir forests helped them recover.

q.t: Your Aadhaar card carries which symbol?
q.e: The three-lion emblem appears on official documents.

q.t: A school emblem that needs a paragraph of explanation is…
q.e: A symbol should say a big idea at a glance.

q.t: A child learning coding and Bharatanatyam shows…
o: New things can sit alongside old ones
q.e: Modern changes add to tradition rather than replacing it.

q.t: 'Diversity makes our country stronger' is like a forest because…
o: Many skills and traditions solve problems in many ways
q.e: Variety is a strength in both.

q.t: Which is India's biggest digital ID system?
q.e: Aadhaar is the world's biggest digital ID.

q.t: Which pair of music styles and instruments is correct?
q.e: Sitar and shehnai are Hindustani; mridangam is Carnatic.

q.t: A watermark becomes visible when held to light because…
o: Thinner parts of the paper let more light through
q.e: The paper is made thicker and thinner in a pattern.

q.t: India is the world's largest…
q.e: India is the world's largest democracy.

q.t: Which is NOT one of the flag's meanings?
q.e: Green stands for growth and prosperity, not courage.

q.t: Why do national symbols get taught and displayed repeatedly?
o: Everyone must agree on their meaning
q.e: The agreeing is the whole mechanism of a symbol.

q.t: If one kind of tree fails in a forest…
q.e: Variety means one failure doesn't end everything.

q.t: Ayurveda and yoga are…
o: Thousands of years old and still practised
q.e: Old traditions continue alongside modern science.

q.t: The 'threads' metaphor for India means…
o: Many threads make a strong, colourful fabric
q.e: Many different threads woven together are stronger than one.

q.t: Why is using money a 'design' question?
o: Money must work for every citizen
q.e: Raised marks make notes usable by people who can't see.

q.t: The three lions of the emblem stand for…
q.e: They stand in for those ideas on official documents.
